tweets: A boulder the size of a house once saved a 1,200-year-old temple from being wiped off the map. 🏔️
Kedarnath Temple sits at 3,583 m in the Garhwal Himalayas, near the source of the Mandakini river — one of the highest points of continuous Hindu pilgrimage on Earth.
Legend ties it to the Mahabharata: after the Kurukshetra war, the Pandavas sought Shiva's forgiveness. He fled in the form of a bull and dove into the earth — his hump is worshipped here.

The current stone temple is traditionally dated to around the 8th century CE, linked to the sage Adi Shankaracharya. Massive grey stone slabs are locked together without mortar — built to survive Himalayan winters and avalanches.

In June 2013, flash floods and landslides devastated the town around it. The temple itself stood — a giant rock reportedly split the debris flow and shielded its walls. Stone, faith, and geography, still standing. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
